topic: What interference management strategies are critical for full-frequency reuse in multi-beam LEO satellite constellations?
consensus_response: To manage inter-beam interference (IBI) in full-frequency reuse multi-beam LEO satellite constellations, linear precoding techniques can be employed at the transmitter to exploit spatial degrees of freedom. However, CSI requirements and computational complexity limit the effectiveness of linear precoding. To balance spectral efficiency and interference mitigation, Hybrid Precoding with Machine Learning (ML) is proposed, which combines linear precoding with ML algorithms to adaptively manage IBI in real-time. This approach leverages the flexibility provided by reconfigurable phased arrays and ML-based algorithms to adjust element patterns and mitigate IBI.
reference_context: Aggressive frequency reuse schemes have been considered for high-throughput wireless communications, but inter-beam interference becomes a critical issue. Linear precoding techniques can manage IBI, but are hindered by CSI requirements and computational complexity. Reconfigurable phased arrays with ML-based algorithms can adaptively adjust element patterns to mitigate IBI.
